title: Qareeb
tagline: Dual-app, location-based delivery platform with separate customer and driver (captain) experiences.
overview: Qareeb ("nearby" in Arabic) is an on-demand delivery platform built as two coordinated Flutter apps — one for customers placing requests, one for drivers (captains) fulfilling them — sharing a common set of packages for maps and data models.
problem: Delivery requests needed real-time location matching between customers and nearby drivers, with two very different UI needs depending on whether you're requesting or fulfilling a delivery.
solution: Rather than one app with role-switching, I built two focused Flutter apps sharing common packages: a maps package for location logic, a models package for shared data types, and supporting packages for UI elements used in both apps.
architecture: BLoC-based state management in both apps, with shared Dart packages (map_qareeb, qareeb_models) published as git dependencies so location logic and data models stay consistent without duplicating code between the customer and captain codebases.
features: Real-time location tracking and driver matching
Separate, purpose-built UI for customers versus drivers
Shared map and data-model packages to avoid logic drift between apps
Order/request lifecycle from creation to completion
challenges: Keeping two independently evolving apps consistent by extracting genuinely shared logic into packages instead of copy-pasting
Handling live location updates efficiently without draining battery or overloading the backend
lessonsLearned: Extracting shared packages early (models, maps) prevents the two apps from silently diverging as features get added independently
futureImprovements: In-app chat between customer and driver
Estimated arrival time based on live traffic data
results: Two coordinated production apps sharing a consistent location and data layer
